A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPIFA work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison despite relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaMA compression experiments, WikiText2 perplexities, fine-tuning outcomes, measured GPU efficiency and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds C4, SuperGLUE, LLM-Pruner, compression-resource and ESPACE experiments in Appendices C–G.

M1.justification: The PIFA representation, M reconstruction objectives and updates, regularization, and inference procedure are retained. Algorithms 1 and 2 are moved and renumbered. Applying the existing components to ESPACE introduces no documented change to their procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates model quality on WikiText2 and uses C4 in fine-tuning data. v2 additionally evaluates C4 perplexity with WikiText2 calibration and eight zero-shot SuperGLUE tasks (Appendices C–D), substantially broadening evaluation domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: LLM-Pruner, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated comparator for perplexity and layer efficiency in Appendix E. Appendix G adds four ESPACE pruning-only comparators: MSE, MSE-NORM, GO-MSE and GO-MSE-NORM. The original low-rank and semi-structured comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot SuperGLUE evaluation using accuracy and ReCoRD F1, compression-time and peak-memory measurements with explicit stage boundaries, and structured-layer comparisons at 55% and 70% density. Appendix B.2 also corrects the reported attention-density search from global density minus 1 to minus 0.1; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G/Table 15 adds a substantial component analysis comparing X, X plus PIFA, X plus M, and X plus MPIFA across SVD-LLM and four ESPACE pruning variants. It newly isolates PIFA without M and tests component benefits beyond SVD-LLM. Existing mix-ratio, calibration-size and conditioning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: The original WikiText2 tables, efficiency measurements and plotted results are retained. Tables 8–15 add C4/SuperGLUE scores, LLM-Pruner results, compression costs and component results. For example, the new 50%-density LLaMA2-7B comparisons report C4 perplexity of 52.01 versus 129.8 and SuperGLUE means of 52.9 versus 50.5 for MPIFA versus SVD-LLM.

T1.justification: The factorization identities, parameter and FLOP derivations, reconstruction equations, regularized objective and module-density formula are retained. Appendix A's closed-form derivation and invertibility assumptions are unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's priority claim that comparable performance to semi-structured pruning is achieved 'for the first time.' The central claims about lossless PIFA compression, M's error correction and MPIFA's performance and efficiency remain in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion interprets cross-method results as evidence for plug-in applicability, describes the tradeoff against LLM-Pruner, and explains compression costs through rank searching and CPU staging. It explicitly limits ESPACE evaluation to pruning variants that avoid backpropagation. Existing explanations about overfitting, conditioning and PIFA requiring prior rank reduction remain.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository, newly specifies 2048-token calibration/perplexity evaluation, and details compression hardware, timing scope and CPU staging. Appendix B.2 corrects the density-search value. The existing fine-tuning recipe, including its 1024-token sequence length, remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds references including SLEB, ShortGPT, DISP-LLM, LORD and Dobi-SVD; new appendices discuss ESPACE and evaluated relationships to structured pruning. These extend the existing positioning without replacing its central low-rank versus semi-structured framing. The abstract also drops its first-time priority assertion.

P1.justification: The abstract receives limited editing, affiliations and publication information are updated, acknowledgements are added, and Appendices C–G extend the document. The original section sequence and most existing explanatory prose remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial tabular presentation for C4, SuperGLUE, structured pruning, compression resources and component combinations. It moves the factorization algorithm, original component table and sensitivity plots into the main text, reduces the calibration plots to column width, and reorganizes appendix displays. The eight figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v1 evaluates model quality only on WikiText2 and demonstrates component benefits in LLMs using SVD-LLM's pruning step. v2 adds downstream tasks, C4 evaluation and component combinations across ESPACE variants, addressing substantial gaps in generalization and component attribution. LLM-Pruner and compression-resource comparisons also strengthen practical assessment. ESPACE coverage remains pruning-only and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the expanded validation provides a substantial overall quality gain.
